validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, well-documented asset. Independent corroboration: (1) Oil & Gas Journal, Dec. 2001, reporting Kinder Morgan Energy Partners' $750M purchase of Tejas Gas LLC from InterGen (a Shell/Bechtel JV) -- names it 'Tejas Gas' pipeline, states '3,400-mile intrastate gas pipeline system extending from south Texas to the Louisiana border,' 16 compressor stations (73,585 hp), two storage facilities (100 Bcf working capacity), three processing facilities. (2) Reuters, Feb. 15 2017 (live URL now 401s -- access failure, not a deletion; cited via Wayback capture per standing rule): 'a Kinder Morgan Inc natural gas pipeline exploded... on its Tejas pipeline in a rural area of Refugio, Texas' -- directly names the pipeline AND confirms the sheet's StartLocation county. (3) Oil & Gas Journal, Jul. 2023 (already on the wiki page, re-verified live): Kinder Morgan + Howard Energy 2-bcfd Eagle Ford expansion tying into 'the Tejas pipeline system near Sinton, Texas.' (4) Kinder Morgan's own current corporate operations page confirms Tejas as an active, named intrastate system. Four independent origins (trade press x2, wire service, operator) spanning 2001-2023 -- not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correctly gas transmission; this is GEM's whole-network aggregate for a sprawling KM Texas-Gulf-Coast intrastate system (consistent with how other large TX intrastate systems are tracked in this same batch, e.g. P0203 HPL, P0264 Texas Intrastate System) -- not a misclassification. DUPLICATE: checked against all 44 other rows in the 45-row roster; no clear match. Flagging one structural note for awareness, not a same-roster duplicate: Kinder Morgan's own SEC 10-K filings (FY2013, FY2015) state 'The two largest systems in the group are Kinder Morgan Texas Pipeline and the Kinder Morgan Tejas Pipeline. These pipelines essentially operate as a single pipeline system' and report them ONLY as a combined figure (e.g. FY2015: 5,600 mi / 6.20 Bcf/d combined). 'Kinder Morgan Texas Pipeline' does not appear as a separate row in this 45-row roster, so this is not an internal duplicate within scope -- but if GEM tracks a 'Kinder Morgan Texas Pipeline' row elsewhere in GGIT, that pairing should be checked for consistent treatment. validity.recommendation: Route to Update: GEM's Capacity (120 MMcf/d) is almost certainly wrong by roughly 30x. Verify and correct -- best independent point estimate is ~3.5 Bcf/d (3,500 MMcf/d) for the Tejas system specifically.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's sheet value is Capacity=120.00 MMcf/d. Every independent source found describes Tejas at Bcf/d scale, not MMcf/d: (1) Oil & Gas Journal, Dec. 2001 (at the time of the Kinder Morgan acquisition): 'Tejas Gas, with a transportation capacity of 3.5 bcfd...' -- an exact, explicit figure. (2) Kinder Morgan's own current operations page (this is the wiki's own citation #3, re-verified live): states Tejas alone has 'a transportation capacity of 3.5 bcfd' -- i.e. the SAME 3.5 Bcf/d figure, 20+ years apart, from two independent origins (1990s-2001-era trade press vs. present-day operator disclosure). (3) SEC 10-K filings (KMI FY2013, FY2015) report the combined Kinder Morgan Texas + Tejas system (KM's own 10-K says these 'essentially operate as a single pipeline system') at 5.5-9.3 Bcf/d combined design/peak capacity, and separately note combined CO2-removal TREATING capacity of ~180 MMcf/d and liquids-processing capacity of 85-685 MMcf/d -- i.e. even the ancillary TREATING capacity for the combined system exceeds GEM's 120 MMcf/d TRANSPORT figure for Tejas alone. This is not a close call or a segment-vs-network nuance: three independent source families (2001 trade press, present-day operator page, SEC filings) all place transport capacity roughly 30-75x above the sheet value. Per standing rules I am NOT auto-applying a new number (a reconciliation/spec finding is a candidate for Update, not an applied edit) -- flagging for correction, best point estimate ~3,500 MMcf/d per the two independent 3.5-bcfd citations above.

validity.recommendation: Route to Update: verify LengthKnown. Sheet's 3,244 mi (5,221 km) is lower than the 3,400 mi reported at the 2001 Kinder Morgan acquisition and well below Kinder Morgan's current stated ~3,800 mi -- an odd trajectory for a system that has only grown via acquisition (South Shore, Mission Valley, La Salle, Red Gate, Southcross).
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet: LengthKnown=5221.00 km (3,244 mi). Oil & Gas Journal, Dec. 2001 (acquisition article): '3,400-mile intrastate gas pipeline system.' Kinder Morgan's own current operations page: 'approximately 3,800 miles of pipeline,' and separately describes 'recently acquired' South Shore, Mission Valley, La Salle, and Red Gate Pipelines folded into the system (plus KM's 2019 Southcross Energy acquisition, per KM's own investor-relations press release). A system growing via repeated bolt-on acquisitions should trend UP over time (3,400 mi in 2001 -> 3,800 mi today), yet GEM's current figure (3,244 mi) sits BELOW even the 2001 pre-acquisitions baseline. That is inconsistent with the acquisition history and suggests either a transcription/unit error, a stale figure from a different vintage, or a segment redefinition -- not something I can resolve to a specific correct number without more digging, but it does not read as a simple stale-vs-current gap. Flagging as a genuine spec discrepancy rather than a routine staleness note.

validity.researcher_notes: Sheet: StartYear1=1953. I could not find any independent source (OGJ 2001 acquisition article, OGJ 2023, Kinder Morgan's current site, SEC 10-K filings, Reuters) that states or corroborates a 1953 founding/in-service date for Tejas. Every web result surfacing '1953' traces back to gem.wiki's own page text (the same 'extends from south Texas along the Mexico border... north from the Houston area to east Texas' phrasing that appears verbatim on gem.wiki appears in search-engine summaries, i.e. circular). The 2001 OGJ acquisition piece, which is the most detailed contemporaneous account of Tejas's corporate history (InterGen -> Kinder Morgan), does not mention a 1953 origin at all. This does not mean 1953 is wrong -- Texas intrastate gas systems of this vintage commonly do trace to the 1950s -- but it is currently an UNCONFIRMED, GEM-only claim and should not be treated as sourced.

fills.researcher_notes: OGJ's Jul. 2023 article describes an active 2-bcfd expansion of the operating Tejas system (completion Q4 2023); Kinder Morgan's current operations page lists Tejas as a presently operating intrastate system. Two independent, current sources confirm 'operating' status.
Both sources unambiguously describe Tejas as a natural gas (not NGL/oil) transmission system.

Kinder Morgan (via its wholly-owned subsidiary Kinder Morgan Tejas Pipeline LLC) has owned/operated Tejas at 100% since acquiring it from InterGen in Dec. 2001/closing Q1 2002 (OGJ), and KM's own current operations page confirms present-day ownership. No sign of a change in ownership since.

EndLocation=Fort Bend County has NO independent corroboration I could find -- every source describing Tejas's geographic extent (OGJ 2001: 'to the Louisiana border'; gem.wiki's own prose: 'north from the Houston area to east Texas') describes a sprawling multi-directional intrastate network, not a single point terminus, and none names Fort Bend County specifically. This is consistent with the known segment-vs-network granularity issue for large TX intrastate aggregates (this row, like P0264 'Texas Intrastate System Gas Pipeline,' compresses a network into one start/end pair) -- not necessarily wrong, but unconfirmed.

Two material spec concerns staged: Capacity (120 MMcf/d) is contradicted ~30x by independent sources agreeing on ~3.5 Bcf/d, and Length (3,244 mi) sits below even the pre-acquisition 2001 baseline of 3,400 mi against a current ~3,800 mi -- both routed to Update, not auto-applied.
